boundary_analysis.invariant: Full runtime extent and page-rounding arithmetic
boundary_analysis.evidence: Positive CInt size converts to usize without sign extension. On x86_64 length <=2147483647, pages <=524288 and pages*4096 <=2147483648; additions/products and CInt page-count cast cannot overflow. Copies length rather than fixed fp_regs_struct extent. The actual supported boot-stable XSAVE extent remains a caller contract.

No Rust references over the Thread allocation are manufactured: fp_regs loads/stores use raw field places. Caller retains both lifetimes and exclusive destination ownership; source/destination extent must not overlap, matching original memcpy. Null source performs no allocation/write. Null threads fail -EINVAL. Failed allocation returns -ENOMEM with original destination pointer/data intact. Successful allocation zeroes rounded extent, stores ownership in destination, then copies; no later recoverable error can leak the allocation. Existing buffers retain untouched page tail.

Rust bridge declaration matches production C int/int/unsigned-long/int/int/unsigned-long/char*/int and pointer return. Uses pages,0,2,-1,0,ULONG_MAX,read-only CPU_FILE diagnostic pointer,line; matches existing allocator arguments. Rust source Thread repr(C) and existing assertions compile; fixture additionally asserts size5568 align64 fp_regs4784. C fixture uses a layout stand-in, so production-header/compiler ABI must still bind during exact image build.

Only production x86 caller is kernel/process.c clone_thread copy_fp_regs(org,thread), immediately branches any nonzero result to free_fp_regs. That label invokes existing process_release_fp_regs_result(thread,release_fp_regs), then frees thread pages. Null/invalid configuration errors introduce safe rejection for states outside valid saved-source lifecycle; invalid C behavior is not used as an oracle. Parallel scheduler admission modifications are excluded from this review.
